native/resume-token/current: Production replays a resume as a change log: a global boundary follows the replayed commit before CURRENT (FS-LISTEN-SDK L1, runs nmuuicyas and nmuukwo6n, both). fireemu diffs the target's state at the token against the current one and sends no boundary before CURRENT. A boundary before a target's CURRENT raises no snapshot in a client, so the documents and the place of CURRENT agree. Production's replay shape also varies by row (resume-token/older sends two documents and a filter with no boundary between them), so no single rule reproduces it without guessing the server's history window.
native/existence-filter/with-expected-co: Production replays the two commits since the token (a delete and a change that took the document out of the query) with a global boundary after each, as documentDelete, boundary, documentChange with removed target ids, boundary (runs nmuuicyas and nmuukwo6n, both). fireemu sends the same two document messages and no boundary between them; a boundary before CURRENT raises no snapshot in a client. The document messages themselves match (delete, and a change with removed target ids).
native/existence-filter/without-expected: Without an expected count production answers the same resume with an existence filter (count 1) and no document message at all, so the client finds the removals by the count mismatch (runs nmuuicyas and nmuukwo6n, both). fireemu always sends the exact diff, which is where a client ends after the filter and reset path. The SDK sends an expected count on every resume, which is the row above. Reproducing the choice between the two answers needs the server's history window, which is not observable.
